written: 2026-10-14, F7, on the parent's decision, BEFORE any Stage-0 / P6 GPU number exists for any new codeword

decision.H6a: SINGLE CONFIRMATORY TEST: one-sided permutation Spearman(held-out probe rho, r1 VALIDATION specificity z) > 0 across CONFIRMATION codewords, alpha = 0.05, NO multiplicity correction (it is the only confirmatory test of P6).
decision.H6b: DESCRIPTIVE (no longer confirmatory, not in any multiplicity family): Spearman(Zipf, z) across CONFIRMATION codewords reported with a codeword-level bootstrap 95% CI (and its permutation p as a descriptive number), PRE-LABELLED 'UNDERPOWERED' — a non-significant or null-looking H6b may never be described as evidence against a frequency effect. Its repair-sensitivity analyses S1/S2 (AMENDMENT_1 F9) are still reported.
decision.Holm: REMOVED (AMENDMENT_1's Holm over {H6a, H6b} is superseded).

rationale: The Zipf range of the untouched pool is narrow (3.54–4.69), so H6b is underpowered at every attainable confirmation n regardless of correction (AMENDMENT_1 F10: two-sided n=15 power 0.63 at rho 0.8 even before Holm-optimistic gains; needs n>=17 with only 15 available).

Keeping H6b in a Holm family costs only H6a power: at n = 15, rho 0.7 (reliability 0.7), H6a power falls from 0.71 (one-sided alpha 0.05) to 0.58 (conservative Holm alpha 0.025), for no realistic gain on H6b.
Decision taken before any Stage-0 covariate or outcome exists for any new codeword, so it cannot be outcome-driven.
UNDERPOWERED_rule_v3: Replaces AMENDMENT_1 F10's rule. With n_conf = confirmation codewords surviving G1–G3: H6a is PRE-LABELLED 'UNDERPOWERED for rho < 0.8' if n_conf < 15, and 'CANNOT ANSWER' (no confirmation GPU spent; redesign with new codewords) if n_conf < 12. H6b: always 'UNDERPOWERED' (descriptive).
unchanged: Everything else in PREREG_P6 and AMENDMENT_1 (pool, banks, occurrence-gate row exclusions, DEV draw + fill rule, gates G1–G3, primary per-codeword outcome, S1/S2 repair sensitivity, TEST never).
